title: (a + b)²: why the middle term is 2ab
familyTitle: Expanding with (a + b)², (a − b)² and (a + b)(a − b)

knowledge: multiplying two binomials term by term
prerequisites.note: the graph's prerequisite relations for identities were not changed

concept: (a + b)² = (a + b)(a + b). Multiplying every term by every term gives a×a, a×b, b×a and b×b.
a×b and b×a are the same, and there are TWO of them: a² + 2ab + b². The area picture shows them as two equal rectangles.
explanation.visualNote: Reuses ahid's own 'area' visual ({type:'grid', rows:2, cols:2}); labels proposed (the existing visual has none).

workedExamples.prompt: Use the identity (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² to expand (5x + 2)². (5x + 2)² = 25x² + □x + 4. What number goes in the box? (It may be negative.)
lines: The box is the x coefficient: 20

workedExamples.prompt: Use the identity (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² to expand (3x − 8)². (3x − 8)² = 9x² + □x + 64. What number goes in the box? (It may be negative.)
lines: The box is the x coefficient: -48

hints: Write the square as a product of two brackets.
Multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second: four products.
Two of the four products are the same; add them.

Two of the four products are the same; add them.

alternativeExplanation.title: Multiply it out
text: Write (px + q)² as (px + q)(px + q) and multiply each term by each term.
The two middle products come out equal, so the middle term is doubled.
